request.question:
Which pairs of packages call into each other in both directions?

Requested output columns: package_a (string), package_b (string).
Return every requested field using exactly its specified column alias. Preserve complete case-sensitive repository-relative paths and symbol IDs; do not substitute display names. Include all requested counts and provenance fields. Explain the query result in ordinary prose; do not emit placeholder text. These questions concern a static map of open-source Python code. Describe what the query computes and the assumptions it makes; the returned rows are reported separately. Questions asking which files, modules or symbols mean distinct identities, not one repeated row per matching import or call occurrence; preserve occurrence counts only when requested. Caller/callee graph questions include methods as well as standalone functions unless a symbol kind is explicitly restricted. Use files.is_test for test-file classification; test_links describe associations, not the complete set of test files. Use DOUBLE or DECIMAL, rather than single-precision REAL, for percentage calculations.
List each pair once, with the lexicographically smaller package in package_a.

events.sql: WITH edges AS (SELECT DISTINCT caller_file.package AS caller_pkg, callee_file.package AS callee_pkg FROM auto_ontology_code.code.calls AS c JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS caller_symbol ON c.caller_symbol_id = caller_symbol.symbol_id JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.files AS caller_file ON caller_symbol.file_id = caller_file.file_id JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.symbols AS callee_symbol ON c.callee_symbol_id = callee_symbol.symbol_id JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.files AS callee_file ON callee_symbol.file_id = callee_file.file_id WHERE c.resolution IN ('same_file', 'imported', 'method_on_self') AND c.callee_symbol_id IS NOT NULL AND caller_file.is_test = FALSE AND callee_file.is_test = FALSE AND caller_file.package <> '' AND callee_file.package <> '' AND caller_file.package <> callee_file.package) SELECT e1.caller_pkg AS package_a, e1.callee_pkg AS package_b FROM edges AS e1 JOIN edges AS e2 ON e1.caller_pkg = e2.callee_pkg AND e1.callee_pkg = e2.caller_pkg WHERE e1.caller_pkg < e1.callee_pkg ORDER BY package_a, package_b

answer.response: This query finds pairs of Python packages that call into each other in both directions, using resolved internal call records and excluding files classified as tests. It resolves both the caller and callee symbols to their files so each call edge can be attributed to a package, keeps only edges where the two packages differ and neither package is empty, and then joins the edge set to its reverse to confirm mutual calling. Each qualifying pair is returned once, with the lexicographically smaller package listed first as package_a and the larger as package_b, ordered by that pair.

gold_sql:
WITH edges AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT fa.package AS from_package, fb.package AS to_package
  FROM code.calls c
  JOIN code.symbols a ON a.symbol_id = c.caller_symbol_id
  JOIN code.files fa ON fa.file_id = a.file_id
  JOIN code.symbols b ON b.symbol_id = c.callee_symbol_id
  JOIN code.files fb ON fb.file_id = b.file_id
  WHERE fa.package <> fb.package AND NOT fa.is_test AND NOT fb.is_test
)
SELECT e1.from_package AS package_a, e1.to_package AS package_b
FROM edges e1
JOIN edges e2 ON e2.from_package = e1.to_package AND e2.to_package = e1.from_package
WHERE e1.from_package < e1.to_package
ORDER BY package_a, package_b;
